analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיִּבְרָא, and אֶת marks הָאָדָם as its direct object. The phrase בְּצַלְמוֹ describes humanity as created in God's image. The two following clauses repeat בָּרָא to describe the same act.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and no suffix

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּבְרָא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם, the singular verb וַיִּבְרָא identifies אֱלֹהִים as the one who created humankind. The singular suffix in בְּצַלְמוֹ, “in his image,” refers back to the creator.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute, with singular agreement.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּבְרָא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם, אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיִּבְרָא “created,” and אֶת marks the definite noun הָאָדָם “the human” as its direct object.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The singular pronoun אֹתוֹ (“him”) refers back to הָאָדָם. The final clause describes the same referent as זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה (“male and female”) and uses the plural אֹתָם (“them”), showing that the singular noun denotes humankind collectively.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: The parallel phrase בְּצֶלֶם אֱלֹהִים “in the image of God” identifies God as the referent of “his” and describes the likeness in which God created humankind.
analysis.morphology: Preposition בְּ “in” + masculine singular construct noun צַלְמ־ + third-person masculine singular possessive suffix וֹ “his”.

analysis.evidence: בְּצֶלֶם אֱלֹהִים (in the image of God) restates בְּצַלְמוֹ (in his image). The construct noun takes אֱלֹהִים as its complement, identifying God as the one whose likeness the human bears.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed preposition בְּ (in) + masculine singular construct noun, without a suffix.

analysis.evidence: בְּצֶלֶם אֱלֹהִים means “in the image of God.” It restates בְּצַלְמוֹ (“in his image”), whose singular suffix refers to God, the creator named at the start of the verse.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute, with singular reference and no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In בְּצֶלֶם אֱלֹהִים בָּרָא אֹתוֹ, “in the image of God he created him,” the subject carries over from the opening clause, where God creates humankind. The singular object אֹתוֹ refers back to הָאָדָם.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, with no prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: זָכָר is paired with וּנְקֵבָה (“and female”). Together they describe the people referred to by אֹתָם (“them”) in בָּרָא אֹתָם (“he created them”).
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute noun used predicatively, with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add נְקֵבָה under נקב with its sense “female.”
draft.definition: A female, the counterpart to a male.
draft.evidence: Genesis 1:27 describes the humanity God created as זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה, “male and female.”

analysis.evidence: In זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה בָּרָא אֹתָם, “male and female he created them,” נְקֵבָה is paired with זָכָר, “male.” The plural object אֹתָם, “them,” refers to the humans described by both terms.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ־ “and” prefixed to a feminine singular absolute common noun.
analysis.sense: A female, here a female human.

analysis.evidence: In זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה בָּרָא אֹתָם (“male and female he created them”), אֱלֹהִים remains the subject. The plural object אֹתָם refers to the humans described as male and female.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular

draft.change: Add Genesis 1:27 as defining evidence for the existing object-pronoun sense in et.
draft.definition: With a pronominal suffix, אֵת expresses the direct object as a pronoun. Here אֹתָם means “them.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 1:27 shifts from the singular object אֹתוֹ to the plural object אֹתָם when humanity is described as זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה, “male and female.”

analysis.evidence: The repeated בָּרָא links בָּרָא אֹתוֹ, “he created him,” with זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה בָּרָא אֹתָם, “male and female he created them.” The plural suffix refers to the male and female together as the object of “created.”
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle in its suffixed form אֹת־ with the third-person masculine plural pronominal suffix ־ָם.
analysis.sense: With a pronominal suffix, marks the referent of the suffix as the direct object of the verb.
